## Inferred rule (verified on all three demonstrations and the test)
The input contains two corresponding, same-width patterned objects/copies, placed separately in the larger mostly-zero canvas. Align their local bounding boxes and compare cells in the overlapping row-by-row layout. Produce a binary discrepancy mask: output `8` wherever the corresponding input cells differ (including colored-vs-background differences), and `0` wherever they match. Retain the full object width; crop output vertically to the first-through-last rows that contain any discrepancy. Thus output height is the vertical span of disagreement, not necessarily the full object height. Do not copy the input colors into the answer.

The shapes may be irregularly damaged/altered; output records locations of mismatches, independent of the colors involved. Demos establish equal local widths and row alignment, though the two copies can be at different canvas positions.
